confidence_notes: Cuba pricing is volatile and dual-tracked: informal rates, USD-quoted tourist prices, and peso prices all coexist. The food and drink figures are rough. They come from search results for aggregated cost-of-living pages: Traveltables (dated July 2023) and crowd-sourced MyLifeElsewhere pages. Those pages gave beer about $2-2.50, cappuccino about $1-2, an inexpensive meal about $6-9, and a mid-range meal for two about $35. I found no reliable Havana cocktail or wine-by-the-glass prices. Cocktail and wine are set from the beer price and one El Floridita daiquiri listing of about $7 (2024), so they are weakly grounded. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge, not live listings, and I did not search for them. Tourist-facing casas particulares and hotels are typically priced in USD and are volatile.
comparable_city_reasoning: Based on Havana-specific aggregate cost-of-living figures (tourist-oriented paladar and bar pricing) and loosely comparable to low-cost Caribbean and Latin American tourist cities. Tourist-venue pricing is used rather than local peso prices.
